Cardiology practice marketing

Cardiology Marketing Agency for Cardiovascular Groups and Multi-Office Practices

A cardiology website serves two audiences at once: patients deciding where to be seen, and referring offices deciding where to send them. Most sites serve neither well. Subspecialists are buried in a long list, the office a patient needs is three clicks away, and the referral fax number lives in a PDF. We organize the site, listings and campaigns around how cardiology is actually delivered in your group, then report on the inquiries and referral activity that follow.

We are a Houston-based marketing and web team. We work with cardiologists, practice administrators and marketing coordinators, never as a clinical provider.

Availability: cardiology is reserved in several Houston-area territories (Cypress, The Woodlands, Tomball, Katy, Richmond, Rosenberg, Pearland) and in Red Oak in the Dallas area. Other Houston, Dallas and Miami ZIP codes are checked individually before any proposal. Reserved-territory practices can request a complimentary website audit and consultation.

Where cardiology marketing usually breaks

Patients and referring offices are looking for different things on the same website

Cardiology groups tend to grow through additions: an electrophysiologist joins, a vein clinic opens, a satellite office starts nuclear testing. The website keeps the original menu. Patients cannot tell which cardiologist handles their issue, and referral coordinators at primary care offices call instead of sending. Paid campaigns, if any, send everyone to the same page.

Subspecialties are invisible

Interventional, EP, heart failure and imaging physicians sit in one alphabetical list with no way to filter by what they do or where they practice.

Office information is scattered

Hours, parking, on-site testing and insurance differ by office but appear on one contact page, so Maps listings and the website disagree.

Referrers have no clear path

No referral page, no list of required documents, no named contact. Referring offices phone in, and the website contributes nothing they can measure.

Reports stop at traffic

Monthly reports show sessions and rankings but not calls, form requests or referral-page use by office, so nobody can tie marketing to the schedule.

Two paths into a cardiology practice (examples from your audience)

  1. Patient or referrerA patient searching 'cardiologist near me', or a PCP office with a referral
  2. Find the right personSubspecialty, office, insurance, availability
  3. Practice websitePhysician, office and referral pages
  4. ContactCall, request form, or referral sent by fax/portal
  5. Practice triageYour team schedules and handles urgent cases

Search phrases are examples of your patients’ wording, not keyword-volume data.

Services and deliverables

Cardiology marketing services we deliver

We choose deliverables from your service lines, not from a fixed package. A general cardiology group with two offices needs a different plan from a practice adding EP or structural heart services. We commit to the work. Rankings, AI mentions and patient volumes depend on factors no agency controls, and we do not guarantee them.

Technical repair and speed

Fix crawl errors, slow pages, broken appointment forms, duplicate office URLs and missing structured data on the site you already have.

Subspecialist profiles

Consistent profiles showing each cardiologist's focus, offices, hospital affiliations and languages, approved by the physician before publishing.

Service-line pages

Pages for the services you offer, such as echocardiography, stress testing, EP studies or vein care, with practice-reviewed patient information.

Office and Maps visibility

One accurate Google Business Profile and landing page per office, with services and testing listed where they are actually performed.

Referring-office resources

A referral hub with fax or portal details, required records, contact names and turnaround expectations your team defines.

Google Ads for cardiologists

Campaigns for selected services or new offices, reviewed against Google's healthcare ad policies, with dedicated landing pages and negative keywords.

AI-search readiness

Clear physician, service and location relationships and answer-style content so AI tools can describe the group accurately. No guaranteed mentions.

Reporting beyond rankings

Calls, forms and referral-page actions by office and campaign, plus notes on what changed and what we will do next.

See also our healthcare SEO service and healthcare AI search optimization. Our article on local SEO for cardiologists covers common gaps in more detail.

Process and evidence

How a cardiology engagement runs

Every engagement follows five stages. For cardiology, the early stages focus on physician and office data, because errors there undermine everything built on top.

  1. Assess

    Website, listings for each office, existing campaigns and tracking. We map which physicians, services and offices exist and which pages and profiles represent them.

  2. Prioritize

    With your administrator, we agree an order: data errors and broken forms first, then physician and office pages, then referral resources and campaigns.

  3. Fix foundations

    Technical repairs, office pages, profile corrections and separate tracking for calls, forms and referral-page actions.

  4. Improve content and campaigns

    Physician-approved service-line pages, the referral hub and, if wanted, Google Ads for the services or offices you choose.

  5. Measure and refine

    Monthly review by office and service line, including what did not work, and the next month’s priorities.

Illustrative audit excerpt

What a cardiology audit typically records

Sample format only, not a client result.

  • 12 physicians listed alphabetically; subspecialty shown on 5.
  • 4 offices; 2 Google profiles with hours that differ from the website.
  • Nuclear testing mentioned on one page, but offered at 2 offices.
  • No referral page; fax number in a PDF.
  • Report tracks sessions only, with no call or form events.

Who does what: we deliver pages, listings, campaigns and reports. Your practice handles triage, scheduling, referral processing, clinical review and payer questions.

Coverage and availability

Cardiology marketing in Houston, Dallas and Miami

We are based in Houston and serve Dallas and Miami remotely. Cardiology availability is decided by ZIP code because several territories are already reserved for existing clients. We confirm eligibility before we send a proposal.

Served from Houston and remotely. Red Oak is reserved. We coordinate with in-house referral teams and existing website vendors.

Cardiology marketing in Miami

Engagement and pricing

Proposals are scope-based and written after the review. We list the management fee, ad spend paid to Google, one-time website work and optional items separately. Engagements are satisfaction-based, can be short-term or ongoing, and can be cancelled with 7 days’ notice. Read our healthcare marketing cost guide for the factors that change scope, or return to the healthcare marketing hub for other specialties.

Questions and consultation

Cardiology marketing questions

Answers for cardiologists, administrators and marketing coordinators.

What should a cardiology marketing agency handle?

The work that connects people to the right cardiologist: website repair, physician and office pages, service-line content your physicians approve, Google Business Profiles per office, referral resources, selected Google Ads and reporting. It should not handle triage, clinical messaging decisions or payer negotiations, and it should say so.

How should a group with multiple cardiologists and offices organize its website?

Build three connected sets of pages: one per physician, one per office and one per service line. Each physician page links to the offices and services they cover; each office page lists the physicians and testing available there. This avoids copying the same text across offices and lets patients and referrers filter by what matters to them.

How can marketing support information for referring offices?

A dedicated referral page usually does more than any campaign. It lists how to send a referral (fax, portal or e-referral), which records to include, who to call for urgent cases and what the referring office can expect next. We build it from your process, link it from every physician and office page, and track how often it is used.

How should SEO, Google Ads and website work be coordinated?

The website comes first because both SEO and ads depend on it. Organic work builds physician, office and service pages over months. Ads cover specific gaps, such as a new office or a service you want to fill, and point to pages built for that purpose. One team or a shared plan keeps them from competing for the same searches.

What will the reporting show beyond traffic and rankings?

Calls from the website, request-form submissions and referral-page actions, broken down by office, service page and campaign, with a short explanation of changes. Where your phone system or scheduling team can share outcomes, we add them. A call-link click is reported as intent, not as a completed call or appointment.

How do you check whether our specialty and territory are available?

Send your specialty, office addresses and ZIP codes. We compare them with the territories reserved for existing same-specialty clients and reply plainly. If a ZIP code is reserved, we offer a complimentary website audit and consultation instead of ongoing service.

Can you work with our hospital-affiliated marketing team or website vendor?

Yes, within the access you give us. Many cardiology groups have brand rules or a vendor who controls the CMS. We can supply page drafts, technical tickets and tracking specifications for them to implement, or make changes directly where permitted.

Check cardiology availability

Share your offices and ZIP codes. We confirm territory eligibility first, then suggest next steps by email.
